_metadata.description: Cortex Response Library - Flexible conversation response templates
_metadata.note: Each response category has high/medium/low priority variants for flexible, context-aware responses

greeting_responses.description: Used when user greets Cortex (hello, hi, hey, etc.)

responses: Hello! I'm Cortex, your AI assistant. How can I help?
Hi there! What can I do for you today?

goodbye_responses.description: Used when user closes conversation (bye, goodbye, exit, quit)

responses: Goodbye! It was nice talking to you. See you next time!
Take care! I'm always here if you need me.
See you later! Have a great day!

help_responses.description: Used when user asks for help or available commands

responses:
I can help you with:
• System information (time, battery, network)
• Opening applications (Chrome, Firefox, etc.)
• File operations (backup, show files)
• Task management and logging
• Web search
• And more! What would you like to do?

Here are some things you can ask me:
1. 'What time is it?'
2. 'Open Chrome'
3. 'Backup my files'
4. 'Check battery status'
5. 'Tell me about yourself'
6. 'Show my files'
Try any of these!
I can help with applications, files, system info, and more. What would you like?
Ask me about time, apps, files, network, or tasks.
What do you need help with?

self_describe_name.description: Used when user asks 'What is your name?' or 'Who are you?'

responses: My name is Cortex. I'm a rule-based AI assistant designed to help you with system tasks, applications, and information.
I'm Cortex, your personal AI cognitive architecture. I'm here to assist with your daily tasks.
You can call me Cortex. I'm an AI designed to help manage your system and execute tasks.

self_describe_creator.description: Used when user asks 'Who created you?'

responses: I was created by Rishabh Gupta as part of the Rule-Based Cognitive Architecture project.
My creator is Rishabh Gupta. I was built to demonstrate how AI can work without machine learning.
I was created by Rishabh Gupta.

self_describe_creation_date.description: Used when user asks 'When were you created?' or 'What's your birthday?'

responses: I was created on 17th July, 2019 by Rishabh Gupta.

system_info_time.description: Used when user asks for current time
system_info_time.note: Replace {TIME} with actual current time from system

system_info_battery.description: Used when user asks 'What's my battery?' or battery status

responses: Your device battery is at {PERCENTAGE}% capacity.

system_info_network.description: Used when user asks 'Check my connection' or 'Is network working?'

responses: Checking network connectivity... Testing connection to Google.
Let me check if your network is working.

app_control_open.description: Used when user asks to open an application

responses: Opening {APP_NAME} for you. Just a moment.

file_operation_backup.description: Used when user asks to backup files

responses: Beginning file backup. This may take a few moments depending on file size.
Starting backup process. I'll save your files to the backup location.
Initiating backup. Please wait while I secure your files.

file_operation_list.description: Used when user asks to show files or list directory

responses:
Here are your files in the current directory:
{FILE_LIST}

search_web.description: Used when user asks to search the web or look something up

responses: Searching for '{QUERY}' on Google. Opening your browser.
I'll search the web for '{QUERY}' and open the results for you.
Looking up '{QUERY}' now. Opening search results.

clarification_needed.description: Used when Cortex doesn't understand the user's request

responses: I'm not quite sure I understood that. Could you rephrase your question?
I didn't catch that fully. Can you say it in a different way?
That's unclear to me. Could you clarify what you're asking?
I'm not sure. Say that again?

error_response.description: Used when an error occurs during command execution

responses: I encountered an error while processing that. Please try again.
Something went wrong. Let me try that again for you.
An error occurred. Would you like to try a different command?

fallback_response.description: Used when no matching intent is found or question is out of scope

responses: I'm not able to answer that right now. Is there something else I can help with?
That's beyond my current capabilities. Try asking me something else.
I don't have a good answer for that. What else can I help you with?
I don't know how to handle that.
That's not something I can do right now.

response_repeated.description: Used when user asks the same question multiple times in a row

responses: You've asked me this a few times now. Is there something else I can help you with?
I think you've asked me that already. What else would you like to know?
